items.title: Phil Woods interviewed by Monk Rowe, Delaware Water Gap, PA, November 8, 1999
items.q: I was more smitten with Dolphy. He was a dear friend.

ctx.x: Do you feel jazz is healthier today than it has been in the past?

No, not really healthier. I think it’s become — I don’t mean to paint a bleak picture — but jazz seems to have lost its cutting edge, it seems to be in a regressive mode activated © Fillius Jazz Archive -2-

somehow. I mean jazz just goes on, and it’s never been so alive and well, we’ve never had so many kids playing music, and this is a positive thing. I don’t mean to negate the import of a kid picking up an instrument because if he’s got an instrument in his mouth he’s probably less liable to buy an assault rifle. I mean I think music is good.
